I’ve been asked to check for new files having a manufacturer clause. Can you add one here?
Done
Why does the CMM have access to each Aegis board?  And do we need/want this in the CMM inventory model?
Yes, it comes from the RTP requirement.
Is the harma board EEPROM accessible to the CMM  as well? That might be a better solution to show the secondary inventory connected.

There are two EEPROMs on the Aegis Board, one for Harma (compute blade) and one for CMM (chassis manager). Both contain the same FRU data to prevent conflicts when accessed by the BMC.

We received a request from the RTP team stating that both Harma and Minerva need to display this information. To achieve this, we use the same probe conditions based on `BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME` and `PRODUCT_MANUFACTURER`, while distinguishing between Harma and Minerva using the SCM.

Since Harma only needs to represent a single Aegis board at a time, whereas Minerva must display all 16 compute blades connected to I2C buses 24-39, we plan to use names such as "Minerva Aegis 1" or "Minerva Aegis 13" to indicate the blade locations in the rack.

>We received a request from the RTP team stating that both Harma and Minerva need to display this information. To achieve this, we use the same probe conditions based on BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME and PRODUCT_MANUFACTURER, while distinguishing between Harma and Minerva using the SCM.

Please copy openbmc_compute@meta.com on this request.  I don't understand why they're expecting every piece of inventory to show up in the CMM but it is seeming to be adding confusion.
Minerva is still under discussion, so we will implement Harma FRU first.
Friendly ping for review.

Minerva and Harma are different meta systems, and it can plug into both? So why does it have 'Minerva' in the board product name?  Also applies to the filename.

What even is an Aegis card?

Aegis is an accelerator module. Harma is the compute card (BMC) which is connected to the aegis board. But the EEPROM has an I2C connection to the chassis manager (Minerva) as well. So, its not that it plugs into either, but it is the same card being reported (in duplicate) by both BMCs (Patrick's query).
Also, to add confusion "Minerva" is the program name and it is also the name of BMC "system" for the chassis controller (CMM).  "Harma" is the compute card that "Aegis" plugs into.
@spinler@us.ibm.com If there are no further questions, could you please proceed with merging the commit?
